juju · Phase 4 · Flutter SDK

Three error channels, one report

A Flutter app usually keeps running after an uncaught Dart error: a broken widget turns into a grey box, a failed future prints to the log. That makes errors easy to miss. Flutter reports them through three different channels, and juju_flutter listens on all of them.

Try it

Which hook catches it?

Pick where an error is thrown, and whether the app runs inside Juju.runZoned. The answer changes, and that's the part of Flutter error handling that surprises people most.

Where is the error thrown?
Is the code running inside Juju.runZoned?
Reported byFlutterError.onError
Event tagmechanism: flutter_error
The app stillshows the error widget

Framework errors always go to FlutterError.onError, zone or not: Flutter catches them while building and reports them itself.

How it differs from React Native

No crash, but the queue still has to survive

In React Native a fatal JavaScript error ends the app, so the SDK has to save the report in the moment before it dies. Flutter doesn't kill the app for a Dart error, so there's no such race. Saving the queue still matters, for two other reasons:

  • The OS kills backgrounded apps to free memory, without warning.
  • Users swipe apps away, often right after something went wrong, and often while offline.
What every hook doesReport the error, then call whatever handler was installed before. Flutter's own console output, the error widget and the app's own handlers all behave exactly as they did without juju. The platform dispatcher hook returns the previous handler's answer, or false ("not handled") so Flutter still prints the error.
Stack traces

Two kinds of Dart trace

Symbolic (normal builds)

Debug, profile and normal release builds keep function names and lines. Frames from your own package count as app code; Flutter's and Dart's don't.

// from the Android release build
checkout             package:juju_example/main.dart:56   app
BrokenCartPage.build package:juju_example/main.dart:175  app
StatelessElement.build package:flutter/…/framework.dart  -
Element.rebuild        package:flutter/…/framework.dart  -

Non-symbolic (--split-debug-info)

Obfuscated builds print addresses only. juju keeps the build_id and the raw trace, so symbolication (Phase 5) can turn them back into code.

// real output from an AOT build with --dwarf-stack-traces
build_id: 'b4485c2e0287804e97e466d035d1c91c'
#00 abs 000000010780cc67 virt 0000000000044c67
    _kDartIsolateSnapshotInstructions+0x34c67
#01 abs 00000001078181ff virt 00000000000501ff …

Set appPackages: {'shop'} to your pubspec name to be exact about which frames are yours. Without it, every package except Flutter's own and a few well-known ones counts as app code.

Offline queue

How an event gets from the phone to juju

  1. The hook builds the event and gives it an id. Every retry reuses that id, so the server can tell a retry from a new error.
  2. The queue is written to juju_queue.json in the app's support folder: first to a temporary file, then renamed over the real one. A rename is atomic, so a kill mid-write leaves the old file intact rather than half-written.
  3. After 5 seconds, or 20 events, the batch is sent, gzipped when it's over 1 KB.
  4. If the send fails, retry after 1 s, 2 s, 4 s… up to 60 s, with jitter, and never sooner than the server's Retry-After.
  5. When the app goes to the background, save and send now. When it comes back, retry straight away.
  6. On the next launch, load the saved file before saving anything new, then send what it held.
Why load before savingIf an error happened in the first moments after launch and its save ran first, it would overwrite the events left by the previous run before they were read. Every save waits for the load. A test fails if this rule is removed.
Using it

Setup in an app

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:juju_flutter/juju_flutter.dart';

void main() => Juju.runZoned(() async {
      WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized();
      await Juju.init(JujuOptions(
        dsn: 'https://pk_...@juju.example.com/1',
        release: 'shop@1.4.0+12',
        appPackages: {'shop'},
      ));
      runApp(MaterialApp(
        navigatorObservers: [Juju.navigatorObserver], // screen changes
        home: const HomePage(),
      ));
    });

final api = Juju.httpClient(); // an http.Client that records requests
  • Everything goes inside Juju.runZoned, including ensureInitialized and runApp, so the Flutter binding and the app share one zone. Inside it, print() lines also become breadcrumbs.
  • Breadcrumbs never record request or response bodies, or query strings, which often carry tokens.
  • No native plugin. Device details come from Dart and Flutter's own APIs, so installing needs nothing beyond flutter pub add.
Verification

Tested on devices, not just in tests

Flutter has no release mode on the iOS simulator: release builds are compiled ahead of time for real devices only. So the release-build check ran on the Android emulator, and iOS was checked in debug mode.

CheckAndroid 17 emulator, releaseiOS 26.5 simulator, debug
Framework, async, zone and handled errors each arrive with their tagpasspass
Flutter still prints the unhandled errorpass (seen in the device log)not checked
Killed while offline, then reopenedlog: "restored 4 event(s)"; all 4 sent in one request 1.9 s after launchjuju_queue.json held 4 events; all sent, then the file was deleted
No duplicates16 events stored, 16 distinct ids

The automated suite has 48 tests, using real Dart traces as fixtures. Two were checked by breaking the code on purpose: dropping the previous handler, or the load-before-save rule, makes them fail.

Found on the devices, fixed afterwards

FormatException: FormatException:

Many Dart errors repeat their type in toString(). The repeat is now dropped from the message.

335 frames

Flutter's widget trees make deep stacks. The SDK now keeps the first 50 and last 200 before sending, as the server would.

CE2A.260420.019 dev-keys

On Android, Dart's OS "version" is a build id. It's now stored as os.build; the version is only set where it's really there (iOS).

INTERNET permission

Flutter's template grants network access only in debug. A release build needs it in the main manifest, or it silently can't send.

Limits

Not covered yet

  • Release mode on iOS, which needs a physical device. No physical device was tested on either platform.
  • Device model and Android OS version need a native plugin.
  • Obfuscated builds end to end. The parser is tested with a real non-symbolic trace, but turning addresses back into code is Phase 5.
  • Flutter web, errors in other isolates, and native crashes in Swift or Kotlin.
